indicators.research_note: No statute or binding regulation found that requires Belgian government data, or classified data, to be stored or processed under national or EU jurisdiction. Checked: the Law of 11 December 1998 on classification (via the etaamb.openjustice.be copy of the Moniteur belge), which sets classification degrees and clearances but has no hosting-location clause; and the G-Cloud service catalogue. The catalogue says sensitive services are hosted in state data centres 'pour lesquels l'indépendance de l'État envers des tiers doit être garantie', but that is programme policy, not law. The implementing Royal Decree of 24 March 2000 and the Belgian NIS2 law (2024) were not reached: ejustice.just.fgov.be rejects scripted requests, and the web-search budget was used up. Silence, so the value is unknown.

review.reason: No claims were cited, and nothing I checked shows a statutory hosting-jurisdiction requirement, so unknown stands.

indicators.research_note: The classification levels are defined in a statute, the Law of 11 December 1998 on classification and security clearances (Art. 4). The quote is from the original text as published in the Moniteur belge on 7 May 1999, taken from the etaamb.openjustice.be copy because the official ejustice portal rejects scripted downloads. Later amendments, such as any added RESTREINT level, were not checked. They would not change the value.

review.reason: Both quotes appear word for word in the etaamb copy of the Law of 11 December 1998, whose Art. 4 defines the TRES SECRET, SECRET and CONFIDENTIEL levels in a statute.

indicators.research_note: No Belgian cloud certification requiring immunity from non-EU law (SecNumCloud-type) was found, and no source saying that none exists. The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium site (ccb.belgium.be), the national cybersecurity certification authority, returned HTTP 403 to scripted requests, and the web-search budget was used up. The G-Cloud catalogue sets no certification requirement. Silence, so the value is unknown.

review.reason: No claims were cited and no source establishes a SecNumCloud-type certification either way, so unknown stands.

indicators.research_note: The Belgian Trusted List names FPS Policy and Support (BOSA), a federal public service, as the qualified trust service provider for Belgium Root CA6, eSeal CA Gov, eSign CA eID and the government timestamp units. The subject is 'Kingdom of Belgium - Federal Government', with FPS Home Affairs as CA/RA. The Citizen CA CPS v1.4 is an older document: it says Certipost ran the Citizen CA 'on behalf and for the account of the Belgian authorities', while the authorities stayed CSP for the Belgium Root CAs. The current trusted list shows the eID signing CA now under BOSA. Private qualified TSPs (Certipost, DigiCert/QuoVadis, GlobalSign, Belgian Mobile ID) also appear on the list, but the government root is state-operated.

review.reason: tsl.belgium.be could not be reached (SSL error and socket closed), so the two trusted-list quotes are unverified; the Citizen CA CPS does contain 'The Belgian authorities are the CSP responsible for the Belgium Root CAs', which on its own establishes a state-operated root.

claims.quote: De eID is de elektronische identiteitskaart die wordt uitgereikt aan elke Belg ouder dan 12 jaar.
claims.quote_english: The eID is the electronic identity card issued to every Belgian over the age of 12.
claims.title: eID

indicators.research_note: The national eID card is issued under FPS Home Affairs (IBZ), and its certificates chain to the state-run Belgium Root CA (see K1). The CSAM identity and access framework, which hosts the federal authentication service, is a joint initiative of federal public services and social-security bodies. itsme, the widely used mobile ID, is run by Belgian Mobile ID SA/NV, a private company, and is listed as a qualified TSP on the Belgian trusted list. The state-run core scheme (eID card plus CSAM/FAS) supports 'yes'. The eIDAS notified-schemes list on the Commission site is JavaScript-rendered and was not fetched.

review.reason: Both quotes appear word for word: the CSAM page lists only federal public services and social-security bodies as its initiators, and the FPS Home Affairs (IBZ) page describes the eID it issues, so the core scheme is state-operated.

indicators.research_note: G-Cloud, the shared cloud of the Belgian federal public sector, is state-managed and has been operational since March 2015. Its catalogue marks IaaS (VMaaS, StaaS), housing, backup, FEDMAN/FEDWAN and CSAM services as 'En service'. It is a hybrid model that also uses private public-cloud providers, so not every workload runs on state infrastructure. The home-page text appears to date from G-Cloud's launch, but the catalogue statuses are current.

review.reason: All three quotes appear on the G-Cloud pages: it has been operational since March 2015, is managed by the State, and its services are 'd'ores et déjà disponibles et largement utilisés', so it is in operation, not just announced.
